messages:
chandra: Heads-up — nightly eval flagged a big spike in structured-output failures for the post-quant int8 build (v2-int8).
nightly-eval-bot: Summary: structured-output promptset failure rate increased from 0.7% -> 9.4% after last nightly. Regression detected at 2024-12-03T03:20:00Z. Link: https://dash.redwood/evals/1738200000
linh: Oof. Is this across models or just int8-packedkv?
sam: Any sample fails? small is fine for triage.
chandra: Only the int8-packedkv artifact. bf16/fp16 runs looked normal.
chandra: Example failing pair (expected JSON parseable -> actual):

```
Expected:
{"answer":"42","source":"kb:article/123"}

Actual:
"{\"answer\":\"42\",\"source\":\"kb:article/123\\n\\n\\u0000\\u0000\"}"
```

chandra: Notice the extra escapes and embedded nulls (\u0000) that cause downstream JSON.parse to blow up.
eva: That looks like double-escaping + some control bytes appended. Could be coming from the runtime serializer in the quant path.
sam: Any recent PRs touching tokenization/serializer/packed-kv layout?
chandra: Yes — PR#5123 changed the packed-kv packing routine to insert sentinel padding (0xff) for alignment and also a small serializer optimization that switches to fast-stable-stringify in the int8 kernels.
linh: Fast-stable-stringify is from the runtime patch — it doesn't sanitize control bytes because we assumed upstream tokenization would never emit them. If packed-kv padding used 0x00/0xff and later code converts binary to escaped unicode sequences, that could explain \u0000.
nightly-eval-bot: Artifact metadata: v2-int8-built-at=2024-12-03T01:10:12Z, commit=aa12b3c, PR=5123
chandra: Triage so far:
- reproducer: run nightly structured-output promptset with v2-int8 on small sample -> 9/100 fails (parse error)
- introspect runtime serializer: int8 path uses fast-stable-stringify with preserveBinary=true flag
- inspect packed-kv padding: padding bytes present in kv buffers before serialization
- hypothesis: fast-stable-stringify + preserveBinary results in explicit \u0000 sequences being inserted instead of being stripped/ignored

sam: Ok. Actionable immediate mitigation?
chandra: Immediate actions we took:
- rolled back the serializer change in int8 artifact (deployed v2-int8-rollback/aa12b3c -> previous good build at commit=aa11f2b)
- disabled int8-packedkv rollout ring (blocked canary and CI deploys)
- added a temporary gating rule: nightly structured-output failure rate >= 2% blocks releases for int8 artifacts
linh: Added unit test that verifies structured-output JSON remains parseable and that serialized kv buffers have no leading padding when preserveBinary=true.
eva: For longer term: we should sanitize binary->string conversions in the serializer and ensure padding bytes are stripped or encoded in a way that doesn't double-escape.
chandra: Proposed long-term mitigations:
- make fast-stable-stringify opt-in per-artifact and default to the safe serializer unless explicit opt-in
- update packing routine to use sentinel 0xFF instead of 0x00 where possible and strip before user-visible serialization
- add nightly-eval threshold gating for structured-output promptset (fail-rate > 1.5% -> auto-fail + page on-call)
- add CI integration test that runs a mini-structured-output prompt set against any quant build before promoting to canary

sam: Do we need a postmortem or is this a low-severity rollback+fix process?
chandra: Filing a short RCA doc. Root cause: serializer + packed-kv padding interaction in int8 kernel path created control bytes that became double-escaped during fast serialization, causing parse failures in structured-output prompts. Immediate mitigations listed above.
linh: I pushed PR#5130 that reverts fast-stable-stringify in int8 and adds sanitization. Test matrix: int8/bf16/fp16 structured-output tests passing locally.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for v2-int8-rollback started (canary-1/3) — blocking full rollout until all checks green.
eva: Let's add an automated alert wire (pager) for the gating rule so we don't rely on manual checks.
chandra: Agree. I'll open a follow-up to wire pager and set the alert threshold to 1.5%.
sam: Thanks — good catch by nightly eval.
nightly-eval-bot: Note: re-run scheduled at 2024-12-03T04:00:00Z to validate rollback.
chandra: Will update the RCA doc and link here when ready. TL;DR: rollback done, canary blocked, gating rule + tests added, long-term serializer hygiene + packing cleanup planned. :white_check_mark:
